results.title: Yemen government forces advance in Bab el-Mandeb with Saudi backing
results.description: Yemen government forces advance in Bab el-Mandeb with Saudi backing Riyadh said on Monday it had attacked hundreds of targets in Yemen to provide air cover for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Yemeni ground forces. Monday 05/10/2026 Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi addresses the nation in a televised speech from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia October 4, 2026. ADEN Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have secured effective control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told Reuters on Monday, though fighting continues with Houthi forces in the area. The government forces advanced rapidly along the coast with heavy Saudi air support to seize key positions in the Dhubab area on the narrowest point of the strait, a vital oil route whose seizure by the Iran-backed Houthis last month sent shockwaves through energy markets. However, while Eryani said the military had seized Dhubab airstrip, located just inland from the strait, and cut off remaining Houthi forces in the area, another government source said fighting continued at a military base near the strait. The Houthis earlier denied that government forces had made gains, describing such claims as “completely untrue”, and they threatened to attack any aircraft flying in Saudi airspace. While recapturing the coastal area around the strait would make it harder for the Houthis to disrupt shipping between the Mediterranean and Indian Ocean, they could still target vessels with drones from positions further up the coast and inland. Meanwhile, the Houthis themselves made important advances near the city of Taiz, gaining sections of a mountain road to leave government forces there besieged, according to five military sources with the Yemeni government. One other government source denied the road had been cut. Fighting has raged along several frontlines in Yemen for weeks after a dormant civil war erupted in a spillover from the US-Iran conflict, with the Houthis seeking to control the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and firing missiles and drones at Saudi cities and infrastructure. Threat to oil exports With Gulf energy exports already restricted by Iran’s closure of the Hormuz Strait, the fighting in Yemen has threatened another major oil export route, pushing up global prices and raising new risks in a region already aflame. The renewed fighting has worsened a humanitarian crisis in Yemen, with the UN migration agency saying on Monday that some 184,000 people had now been displaced since the war resumed. The internationally recognised Yemeni government announced on Sunday the launch of its offensive to recapture territory, with President Rashad al-Alimi swearing to fight “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia”. Saudi Arabia, which arms and trains Yemeni government forces, is backing the military campaign with air power and has sought logistical help from allies to push back the Houthis, restore free traffic in the Red Sea, and end the group’s attacks on its territory. Riyadh said on Monday it had attacked hundreds of targets in Yemen to provide air cover for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Yemeni ground forces. The Yemeni government said it had launched attacks on several fronts including in the province of Sanaa, the Yemeni capital. The Houthi-run health ministry said two people had been killed and seven wounded in strikes on Sanhan and Sa’wan districts in Sanaa province. While the war has raged on several frontlines in Yemen, the heaviest fighting has been in the southwest, both in the coastal area near the strait and in the hills around Taiz, where the Houthis have been battling to surround government forces. Last week Houthi attacks damaged a culvert on the Taiz-Aden road, making it impassable. On Sunday night the group’s fighters made new advances into the town of al-Turbah, sitting atop a high promontory on the road, five government military sources said, though another government source denied this. A Houthi-run news agency on Monday cited a military source as saying the group had driven government forces from the al-Mawasit district of Taiz province, reaching the home of Alimi, head of Yemen’s interim presidential council. Taiz frontline Those fresh advances leave Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city with a population of over half a million and a garrison of thousands of government fighters, surrounded by Houthi forces, the government military sources said. Taiz, nestled among Yemen’s southern highlands, has been on the frontlines since early in the civil war, often under Houthi shell and sniper fire. In al-Mudhaffar area, just outside Taiz but within the area besieged by the Houthis, a long queue formed outside a petrol station on Monday as people waited for fuel and cooking gas canisters. “This is the daily state in Taiz. The suffering of citizens continues in this state,” said one man queuing, Shehab Hazaa. Yemen’s conflict began after the Houthis seized the capital Sana’a in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in the following year with an air campaign aimed at restoring the government and ousting the Iran-backed group. The fighting quickly ground to a bloody stalemate, with most frontlines stalled, leading to a major humanitarian crisis in what was already the poorest Arab state, until a ceasefire was agreed in 2022 that held until this summer. The Houthi movement had launched a surprise offensive last month which captured the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and some 150 km of coast on the Red Sea in a matter of weeks, giving the Houthis new leverage over the international shipping route. That advance also opened a new front in the wider US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran, to which Tehran’s responses included choking oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, to the other side of the Arabian Peninsula. As the Yemeni government, known as the Presidential Leadership Council, made its announcement, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia. They claimed the attacks caused major fires and were in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours. Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all chances of de-escalating the conflict had been exhausted. He thanked Saudi Arabia for its support and called on Yemen’s regional allies and international partners to support PLC forces and institutions. Regional and western officials had said earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to launch an assault on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground. The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh’s operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, sources with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters. The hostilities are compounding Yemen’s humanitarian problem. Three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week. results.title: الذهب يرتفع مع تراجع رهانات رفع الفائدة الأمريكية
results.description: ارتفعت أسعار الذهب عالميًا خلال تعاملات اليوم الإثنين، مدعومة بتراجع توقعات المستثمرين بشأن رفع مجلس الاحتياطي الفيدرالي الأمريكي أسعار الفائدة خلال أكتوبر، بعد صدور بيانات أظهرت تباطؤ نمو الوظائف الأمريكية خلال سبتمبر. وصعد الذهب الفوري 0.2% إلى نحو 4152.19 دولارًا للأونصة، فيما ارتفعت العقود الأمريكية الآجلة 0.4% إلى 4180.30 دولارًا.وجاء تحسن الذهب بعد أن خفّضت بيانات سوق العمل الأمريكية احتمالات رفع الفائدة هذا الشهر إلى نحو 22%، مقارنة بنحو 70% الأسبوع الماضي، مما عزز جاذبية المعدن الذي لا يدر عائدًا مقابل أدوات الدخل الثابت.في المقابل، حدّ ارتفاع الدولار الأمريكي وعوائد سندات الخزانة من مكاسب الذهب، إذ يؤدي ارتفاع العملة الأمريكية إلى زيادة تكلفة المعدن المقوم بالدولار على حائزي العملات الأخرى، بينما تجعل عوائد السندات المرتفعة الأصول التي لا تقدم عائدًا دوريًا أقل جاذبية.وتتجه أنظار الأسواق خلال الأيام المقبلة إلى محضر اجتماع مجلس الاحتياطي الفيدرالي، إلى جانب البيانات الاقتصادية الأمريكية، بحثًا عن مؤشرات جديدة بشأن مسار أسعار الفائدة.وتبقى السياسة النقدية الأمريكية والدولار وعوائد السندات من أبرز المحركات قصيرة الأجل للذهب، فيما توفر المخاوف الاقتصادية والجيوسياسية وطلب البنوك المركزية دعمًا إضافيًا للمعدن كأصل وملاذ.

results.title: احتياطي النفط الاستراتيجي الأمريكي ينخفض إلى أدنى مستوياته منذ 1982
results.description: تراجعت مخزونات النفط الخام في الاحتياطي الاستراتيجي الأمريكي SPR رسميًا إلى قرابة 283.8 مليون برميل، وهو ما يمثل أدنى مستوى لها منذ أكتوبر 1982، وفقاً لوكالة رويترز للأنباء. ويعود هذا الانخفاض الحاد إلى التزام الولايات المتحدة بـخطة سحب وإفراج طارئة جرى تنسيقها مع وكالة الطاقة الدولية، وشملت ضخ نحو 172 مليون برميل في السوق العالمية [...] تم نشر هذه المقالة احتياطي النفط الاستراتيجي الأمريكي ينخفض إلى أدنى مستوياته منذ 1982 للمرة الأولي علي صحيفة الوئام .
